I was {alibi}. I will say that until your shift ends and then I'll say it to whoever replaces you.

I was {alibi}. I don't owe you a theory about a database error. That's IT's job, not mine.

questions.prompt: Walk me through your night again. Slowly.

replies.line: Shift. Close-out. Then {alibi}. Then home. I don't pad my nights with detours, I've got a 7 AM.

Close-out, then {alibi}, then home. That's the sequence. It hasn't changed because the sequence doesn't change.
Close-out. Then {alibi}. Then... home. Yes. Home. Why are you making me do this out loud?
Close-out. Then I doubled back. I {act}. Then home. That's the real sequence. I hate that you made me say it slowly.

questions.prompt: You're lying to me. I can see it on you.

replies.line: What you can see is someone who's missing a shift to sit in a plastic chair. I was {alibi}.
You can see irritation. That's all. I was {alibi} and I resent being read like a mood ring.
You can see that I'm done. That's different from lying. I was {alibi}.
I don't lie. I don't have the time. I was {alibi}. Write it down and stop reading my face.
I was {alibi}. Whatever you think you see is a long shift and bad coffee.
You see stress. Everyone in this building has it. I was {alibi}.
Stop. I was {alibi}. You don't get to decide what my face means.
Yes. You can. I {act}. I've never been bad at this before. I've never had to be good at it.
That's work. Events desk paperwork. I sign ten of those a week. There's a record of what it was for, which I'm guessing you haven't pulled.
It's a desk form. It has a purpose line on it. Read the purpose line.

Work. It's work. If doing my job is evidence now, arrest the whole desk.

questions.prompt: Funny timing on this, don't you think?

replies.line: No. Same-day is how an events desk works. Nobody files a request on Tuesday for a Tuesday.
The timing is the shift. Everything I touch is dated the day I touch it. That's a desk, not a conspiracy.
The timing is boring. It's dated the day I worked because I worked that day. Move on.
If you want funny, look at how long you've spent on a desk form. That's the funny part.

questions.prompt: Convince me this has nothing to do with it.

replies.line: Easy. It's logged, it's cross-referenced, and it's back where it belongs. Call the desk supervisor. She'll confirm it in thirty seconds.
There's a paper trail. I'm the one who built the paper trail. Follow it and you'll end up at my desk, not wherever this happened.
I don't do convincing. I do documentation. The documentation is in the office, and it clears me.
Call the supervisor. I'm not going to beg you to read a form.

questions.prompt: This is your alibi? It doesn't cover the window.

replies.line: It covers where I went. I was {alibi}. I'm not responsible for your window, I'm responsible for mine.
It's a timestamp, not a bodyguard. I was {alibi}. Nobody logs every minute of standing still.
Nothing covers a window except a camera, and you clearly don't have one. I was {alibi}.
I was {alibi}. If your window wants more than that, your window can file a complaint.
The desk supervisor, for the shift. After that, whoever was around. I don't socialize at the end of a shift, I leave.
My supervisor. And my roommate, who was awake and annoyed about it. Those are two actual people.
I've named two people. I'm not going to invent a third to make your form look fuller.
Supervisor. Roommate. Go ask them and stop asking me.

questions.prompt: What did you do after this?

replies.line: Went home. Set two alarms. Slept. I'm not a late night person, I'm a 6:45 person.
I went home. I had an early shift. I don't do 'after' on a work night.
Home. Alarms. Bed. That's the whole glamorous after.
I went to bed. Like an adult with a job. Next question.

questions.prompt: Why is your name on this?

replies.line: Because I'm scheduled. I'm on every list in that building. Try finding one without my name on it.
I work there. My name is on the list because I was assigned. That's how lists happen.
Because I showed up to do my job. Which is more than I can say for half the people on it.

questions.prompt: Being on this got you access, didn't it?

replies.line: It got me a desk and a stop time. Access would've been nice. I've asked for it three times.
I got access to a login and a laminated schedule. If that's what you're calling access, sure.
No. It got me a shift. Everything I can open goes back in a drawer at close-out.
The list gets you a name tag. I'm not going to pretend it's a master key to make you happy.

questions.prompt: Who else on this list would do something like this?

replies.line: I'm not going to do your job for you. But I'd start with whoever doesn't show up on time. Sloppy people do sloppy things.
Half of them, honestly. I don't mean that. I mean I'm not pointing. I just know who leaves early.
I'm not naming anyone. I have to work with these people after you lose interest.
Nobody. Everyone. I don't know. I'm not a witness, I'm a coworker.

questions.prompt: You signed in. When did you sign out?

replies.line: At the end of the block, like always. If the out column is empty, somebody moved the pen. It happens weekly.
When the shift ended. I don't linger. There's nothing to linger for.
End of shift. I've told you the time twice. I was {alibi} ten minutes later.
The second the shift ended. I was out the door before the lights were.

questions.prompt: There's no time out on here. You never left, did you?

replies.line: A blank column means somebody took the sheet before I got back to it. It doesn't mean I slept there.

Because I was scheduled. I don't go to that building for fun. Nobody does.
